title: Checkout 5xx spike after v2.33.0 deploy
symptoms: checkout-api 5xx rose to 22% within 6 minutes of deploying v2.33.0. p99 latency 5.1s. Logs: 'FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections' and 'pgbouncer: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)'.
root_cause: v2.33.0 raised the per-pod SQLAlchemy pool_size from 10 to 25. With 48 pods that is 1,200 client connections against pgbouncer max_client_conn=1000 in front of payments-db.

attempted.note: Made it worse: every restarting pod opened a fresh pool at once, a reconnect storm. 5xx peaked at 31%.

attempted.action: Roll back checkout-api to v2.32.4 (argocd app rollback checkout-api)

postmortem: Any change to DB pool size must be reviewed against pgbouncer max_client_conn x pod count. Added a CI check that fails if pool_size * max_replicas > 800.

title: Checkout errors during HPA scale-out for sale traffic
symptoms: 5xx at 9% while HPA scaled checkout-api from 30 to 70 pods for the Akshaya Tritiya sale. Logs again show 'pgbouncer: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)'.
root_cause: The CI pool check used max_replicas=40 but HPA max had been raised to 80 in a separate PR. 80 pods x pool 10 = 800 + background jobs exceeded pgbouncer limit.

attempted.note: Same reconnect storm as INC-2291. Someone on call did not know the history.

attempted.action: Temporarily cap HPA maxReplicas at 55 (kubectl patch hpa checkout-api)
attempted.note: Errors cleared in 3 minutes, latency stayed acceptable.

attempted.action: Raise pgbouncer max_client_conn to 2000 and default_pool_size to 60
attempted.note: Permanent fix, applied next morning by DBA Arjun Mehta.

postmortem: Restarting checkout-api during pgbouncer exhaustion is actively harmful. The CI pool check now reads maxReplicas from the HPA manifest.

title: OTP SMS delayed up to 14 minutes
symptoms: Kafka consumer group notifications-worker lag on topic otp-events grew to 480k. Logs: 'CommitFailedException: Commit cannot be completed since the group has already rebalanced'.
root_cause: A new SMS provider client added a synchronous retry with 45s backoff. Batches took longer than max.poll.interval.ms=300000, so consumers were kicked from the group, causing rebalance storms.

attempted.note: More consumers than partitions (12); extra pods sat idle and every join triggered another rebalance.

attempted.action: Lower max.poll.records from 500 to 50 and set provider timeout to 5s

postmortem: Never scale a Kafka consumer beyond its partition count. Look for CommitFailedException before scaling.

title: Email receipts lagging
symptoms: Consumer lag on topic receipt-events at 90k and rising. Logs: 'Member consumer-7 sending LeaveGroup request to coordinator due to consumer poll timeout has expired'.
root_cause: Template rendering service slowed down; long batches exceeded max.poll.interval.ms. Same failure mode as INC-2130.

attempted.note: Lag cleared in 7 minutes. Recognised the pattern from INC-2130.

postmortem: Poll-timeout rebalances are the most common cause of consumer lag on notifications-worker.

title: All logins failing with 401
symptoms: 100% of token validations failing. Logs: 'JWKS fetch failed: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid' from auth-service calling idp.internal.
root_cause: The internal IdP TLS certificate expired. cert-manager renewal had been failing silently for 21 days due to a deleted ClusterIssuer secret.

attempted.note: JWKS cache is in memory, restart just dropped the last good keys.

attempted.action: Recreate the ClusterIssuer secret and force renewal (cmctl renew idp-tls -n identity)

postmortem: Added alert on certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds < 14 days. Do not restart auth-service during JWKS failures: it clears the cached keys.

title: Product search returning 429s
symptoms: search-api 429 rate at 35%. Elasticsearch logs: 'CircuitBreakingException: [parent] Data too large, data for [<http_request>] would be [7.9gb], which is larger than the limit of [7.6gb]'.
root_cause: A new 'similar products' aggregation used a terms agg on a high-cardinality field with size 10000 and blew the parent circuit breaker on data nodes.

attempted.action: Feature-flag off similar-products aggregation (flagctl set search.similar_products false)

postmortem: Heavy aggregations must be behind a flag and load tested against production-size indices.

title: Search latency degraded after reindex
symptoms: p95 search latency 1.8s (normal 180ms). Elasticsearch hot threads show merges; JVM heap at 92% on data nodes.
root_cause: Nightly reindex job ran with refresh_interval=1s and replicas=1 instead of refresh -1 / replicas 0 during bulk load.

attempted.action: Pause reindex job and set index.refresh_interval back to 30s

postmortem: Reindex job now sets refresh_interval=-1 and number_of_replicas=0 during bulk and restores after.

title: Checkout slow due to Redis evictions
symptoms: p99 checkout latency 3.4s, 5xx at 2%. Redis INFO shows evicted_keys climbing 40k/min; cart-cache hit rate dropped from 97% to 41%.
root_cause: A promo banner feature stored full product JSON per session in the cart-cache Redis (maxmemory 4gb, allkeys-lru).

attempted.action: Disable promo-banner cache writes via flag (flagctl set checkout.promo_banner_cache false)
attempted.note: Hit rate back to 95% in 15 minutes.

postmortem: Separate Redis instance for experimental features. Alert on evicted_keys rate.

title: Payments DB replica lag 9 minutes
symptoms: Replica lag on payments-db-replica-1 at 540s. Order status pages showing stale 'payment pending'. pg_stat_activity shows a long-running 'VACUUM FULL payments_ledger'.
root_cause: A DBA script ran VACUUM FULL on a 380GB table on the primary during business hours, generating massive WAL.
postmortem: VACUUM FULL on payments-db requires a change ticket and a maintenance window. Use pg_repack instead.

title: Intermittent DNS timeouts from checkout pods
symptoms: 0.8% of calls to payments-gateway fail with 'dial tcp: lookup payments-gateway.prod.svc.cluster.local: i/o timeout'. CoreDNS CPU at 95%.
root_cause: ndots:5 default caused 5 search-domain lookups per external call; a new fraud-check vendor integration multiplied DNS QPS by 6x.

attempted.action: Set dnsConfig ndots:2 on checkout-api and use FQDNs with trailing dot

title: Checkout 5xx after v2.38.0 deploy
symptoms: 5xx at 14% three minutes after v2.38.0 rollout reached 60%. Logs: 'pgbouncer: no more connections allowed (max_client_conn)'. v2.38.0 added a second DB engine for the read replica.
root_cause: The new read-replica engine opened its own pool of 10 per pod, doubling client connections. The CI pool check only counted the primary engine.

attempted.action: Pause the Argo rollout and roll back (kubectl argo rollouts abort checkout-api)
attempted.note: Recovered in 5 minutes. On-call Rohan Das remembered not to restart pods after reading INC-2417.

postmortem: CI pool check now sums every engine's pool. Third pgbouncer exhaustion in five months: always suspect it first when checkout-api 5xx follows a deploy.

title: Stale product images after catalog update
symptoms: Customers see old product images for up to 6 hours. Cache-Control on image responses is 'public, max-age=21600' with no surrogate keys.
root_cause: Image service did not emit Surrogate-Key headers, so catalog updates could not purge specific objects.

attempted.note: Worked, but origin load tripled for 20 minutes. Avoid during peak.

postmortem: Added Surrogate-Key per SKU; use targeted purge.
